intended_object: The chain map (here, a morphism of simplicial R-modules) C_•(X; L) → C_•(X; K) on singular chains with local coefficients, induced by a morphism η : L → K of local coefficient systems. On the summand of a singular simplex σ it acts by η at the initial vertex of σ. Inferred from the docstring and from how `twistedChainsFunctor` uses it.
explanation:
In each simplicial degree n, the map is `Sigma.map (fun σ ↦ η.app (initialVertex σ))`. This is the coproduct over the singular n-simplices σ of the components η_{σ(v₀)} : L(σ(v₀)) → K(σ(v₀)). That is exactly how a morphism of local systems induces a map of singular chains with local coefficients. Naturality in the simplicial direction is proved, not assumed. It holds because η is a natural transformation, so it commutes with the vertex-transport maps used in the face and degeneracy maps.

The map is then used as the action on morphisms of `twistedChainsFunctor`, which is the expected functoriality in the coefficients.

As for generality: the setting (R-modules over a ring R, any topological space X) is the natural one for this construction. Mathlib has no notion of homology with local coefficients, so there is no more general counterpart. The definition is the standard induced map.
